key_insight: Introducing a lightweight Persistent Visual Memory (PVM) module prevents visual information from fading as autoregressive LVLMs generate long text, enabling sustained, on‑demand visual perception throughout generation.
problem_solved: Addresses 'Visual Signal Dilution' — visual attention decays as generated textual history grows, causing LVLMs to lose visual grounding on long generations.
method: Add a learnable Persistent Visual Memory module that runs in parallel to standard cross‑attention, retaining distilled visual representations independent of autoregressive context length.
Provide on‑demand access to persistent visual states via gating/attention so the decoder can re‑query high‑fidelity visual memory at any generation step.
Keep the module lightweight and plug‑in so it can be integrated into existing LVLMs with minimal compute and training overhead.
impact: Enables more stable visual grounding for long-form and iterative multimodal generation, improving reliability of LVLM outputs in tasks that require sustained perception (e.g., multi‑step reasoning, extended descriptions, interactive agents).
visual_elements: Line chart: visual attention strength vs. generated sequence length showing decay without PVM and preservation with PVM.
Architecture diagram: LVLM stack with PVM module in parallel to cross‑attention, highlighting data flow and gating.
Sequence storyboard: an example long‑form generation where PVM preserves correct visual references across many tokens.
Bar chart or table: qualitative/quantitative comparison of grounding fidelity or accuracy with and without PVM (illustrative).
paper_title: Persistent Visual Memory: Sustaining Perception for Deep Generation in LVLMs
paper_authors: Siyuan Huang, Xiaoye Qu, Yafu Li, Tong Zhu, Zefeng He
